---
name: {{name}}-audit-states
description: Hunt one area of an existing codebase for bugs in hidden state (flags, statuses, nullable timestamps, the order of async steps), reproduce them, and turn them into fix items. Use when the user asks for a state-machine audit or bug hunt, or types /{{name}}-audit-states followed by an area.
---
<!-- {{name}}-managed: generated by `{{cmd}} sync`; edits are overwritten -->
Audit one area at a time (the words after the command: a folder or subsystem). If none is named, ask.

1. Run `{{cmd}} new chore "State audit: <area>"`.
2. Hand the hunt to a fresh subagent, read-only on the repo, with any scripts in a temp folder. Its brief: find
   the state machines in <area>, explicit or implicit (flags, nullable timestamps, status strings, maps, the
   order of async steps), with their states, allowed moves and invariants. Find invalid states or moves the code
   can actually reach, including through retries, concurrency, restarts and failures halfway. Reproduce each
   with a script or test: CONFIRMED if reproduced, PLAUSIBLE if only read. Report the sequence, the wrong
   result, file:line and the smallest fix. Skip theory and style. Say in one line which machines are sound.
3. Update `specs/kb/state-machines.md`, kept short: only machines with a confirmed bug or an invariant that
   matters: states, allowed moves, invariants. Each invariant says what enforces it (a test, a database
   constraint, or nothing yet). Offer a constitution article for one that must always hold.
4. Present a ranked list in chat, by impact, in plain words, grouped by fix. Never send the human to read a
   file. Ask which groups to fix.
5. Ship the chore as usual. For each group picked, run `{{cmd}} new fix "<title>"` and plan it: its regression test
   comes first and must fail for the bug's reason.
